assertion_analysis.failure_condition: The negative control's `passed` is derived from filter_hits' own outputs over planted inputs; if filter_hits were to drop a unit-matching hit carrying an extracted/skipped/failed source held by no live name, extracted_kept would be empty and `passed` would be False, so the control does redden on the regression the corrected pass removed. It is independently sourced (planted facts vs code output), not a self-comparison.

owned_population_gate compares the live post read-back against the recorded baseline and asserts owned_shrink == prior_restored + len(new_bindings); if a binding failed to move a name out of dropped_edge/never_bound, owned_shrink would be short of expected and readback_exit would be EXIT=3. The two sides are independent (live graph vs write count). The gate was observed failing on the unscoped variant, recorded in the resume stream as 'read-back gate failed: 10 restored but 21 left the sourceless populations'.

The concurrent-writer attribution is reported, never asserted: run.py:1089 records the runs touched within 1800s and passes gate_ok regardless of which runs they are, so a movement of another population by this node's own writes would pass the gate exactly as an external one does.

0.reason: The JSON record's split, 34 referred with a below-floor candidate and 16 with none, is authoritative and is the figure the plan carries. The one name rendered under the wrong table (fraction_of_neutron_detector_converter) goes to the lead either way, so the total of 50 referrals is unchanged.

findings.text: follow-on: the fragment's tables are split from different stores. render() builds referred_rows from doc['referred_to_lead'] + doc['corrected_referred_to_lead'] (35 rows) and no_cand_rows from doc['corrected_no_surviving_candidate'] (15 rows), while stage_control derives lead_referral_total from the corrected filter (34 with candidates, 16 with none). The name fraction_of_neutron_detector_converter is a first-pass referral whose corrected-filter candidate set is empty, so it is rendered under 'Referred to the lead' with stale first-pass candidates instead of under 'No surviving candidate'; the html summary (line 13) then reads '35 referred to the lead; 15 with no surviving candidate' against the record's 34/16. Both reconcile to the same total of 50 and running total of 67, so the gate and the restored count are unaffected.

follow-on: population_gate is dead code. It is defined at run.py:133-160 and called nowhere (owned_population_gate at run.py:91 replaced it after the unscoped form failed '10 restored but 21 left the sourceless populations'); the superseded guard is left in the driver and reads as a live check a reader may trust.

follow-on: quiet_graph_check records facts and asserts nothing — no condition on its return value can fail, so the 'quiet-graph check' the done_when requires is a record rather than a guard. The same shape was a blocking finding on the sibling node r-20261019T021901634768.

follow-on: spec() (run.py:463-471) re-inlines the DD source dict that imas_codex/standard_names/provenance_rebuild.py:423-430 builds inline inside _fetch_dd_source_paths; no exported owner for that shape exists, so the two can drift and a change to the source spec must be made in two places.
